**TL;DR:**
A popular MOD on the Steam Workshop, named SCAV, contains hidden malicious code. This code causes the game to crash without any warning or error message for players who have been blacklisted by the MOD's author. Embedding such malicious code in a MOD has traditionally been grounds for severe punitive action, including banning the author, in the modding communities of many other games. The purpose of such actions is to set a strong example and rebuild player trust in both the official developers and the community. An issue of this severity should have received immediate and serious attention from the official team, as they are the only ones with the authority and capacity to address it directly. However, the response we ultimately received was as follows:

https://tieba.baidu.com/p/10296590490?see_lz=0

I will excerpt a few passages to illustrate the official team's stance:

"However, this presents a minor issue... If your MOD contains content/code that **[prevents the main game from launching]**, that part may conflict with our MOD agreement and the Steam Workshop agreement. So, I'd like to discuss with you to see if there are any modifications that can be made, or if you have any needs we might be able to assist you with."

"Understood. I've checked the comments section, and it seems some players have engaged in somewhat inappropriate behavior. I can understand the feeling when your labor of love is unreasonably criticized or insulted by others. After all, you are a creator with a large volume of work, high subscription numbers, and significant recognition. It's very likely you encounter all sorts of players, and it's perfectly normal for you to be upset."

For such an author—who insults regular users, blames users for having "too many sharp voices," and selfishly indulges in a "small act of willfulness" at the expense of community trust—why does the official team treat them like they are appeasing a baby, pleading for the code's removal without imposing any penalty, and simply trying to downplay a major issue? As the official representatives, you should be standing with the majority of players, thoroughly purging and denouncing these elements that damage the community environment. But what have you done? You've labeled players who, albeit with sharp wording, pointed out this fundamental principle issue as having "engaged in somewhat inappropriate behavior," while portraying the MOD author who embedded clear malicious code as a "hard-working, unappreciated innocent victim"?

I want to ask the development team one question: What does creating a MOD matter? Should a terrorist who hijacks an entire bus because they dislike one passenger be forgiven simply because they once donated to charity? I have never seen an official team display such poor judgment. A community governed in this manner will only deteriorate, where bad practices drive out good, becoming a feudal society held hostage by small cliques rather than a mutually supportive, sustainable player community.

I still hope the official team will calmly reflect on one question: Is your revenue, your accolades, and your success granted by the majority of players who genuinely want the game to improve, or by a minority of self-indulgent MOD creators? The core game itself is good, but the official handling of this matter has been deeply disappointing due to its indecisiveness. Until the official team addresses this issue with a more serious and resolute attitude, I will not change my review.（AI-translated English）
